clue.text: Consequence of eating? Eat faster, possibly, acquiring temperature

indicators.note: the rearranged letters acquire, or take in, the extra letter
possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the two words are taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Advice that wolfing food might lead to a lingering taste in the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition ends in a question mark because a taste left behind is only loosely a consequence of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The flavour that lingers in the mouth after a meal is something that follows from eating it.

clue.text: French not so good making this decorative item

parts.note: ill describes someone feeling unwell, not so good

explanation.surface: A French-made ornament judged rather poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a gathered strip of fabric added as ornament to clothing or furnishings.

clue.text: Chalet I redecorated on a principled basis

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the adjective, as in an investment made on a principled basis

indicators.note: redecorating rearranges things, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the two words are taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone refurbishes their mountain chalet according to their scruples.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ethical is done according to moral principles.

clue.text: Dump suggestion, after reflecting

indicators.note: a reflection shows the word backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: a pit is an informal word for a squalid place, a dump

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an idea once you have thought it over.
explanation.walkthrough: Dump looks like the definition, since a rubbish dump is a tip, but it is the word to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a piece of helpful advice or a hint.

clue.text: Gloomy planet in East

parts.note: Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun
the word in is used just as it stands

explanation.surface: An astronomer gloomily notes a planet in the eastern sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means sullen or dark in mood, a temperament astrology linked with the planet.

clue.text: Correct edition probed by fellows

indicators.note: the edition is probed, or entered, by the fellows, who go inside it

parts.note: men are fellows, chaps

explanation.surface: Academics poring over an edition to put errors right.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct errors in it.

clue.text: "Extra large" to swamp "small"? Just a bit

indicators.note: the larger pieces swamp, or engulf, the small one, which ends up inside

parts.note: more means extra, as in more food

explanation.surface: A clothes-size quarrel: extra large overwhelming small, yet only a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or mouthful of food.

clue.text: Accident is hard to be located in plan

indicators.note: the letters are located inside the plan, placed within it

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area
the word is is used just as it stands

explanation.surface: A mishap that is hard to find on the plan of a site.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, usually a minor one.

clue.text: Small earthquake setting European city right back

indicators.note: setting the pieces back means reading them in reverse order

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A minor quake sets the Italian capital back a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking of the ground, a minor seismic event.

clue.text: Group of countries stop broadcast on radio

indicators.note: on radio a word is heard, not seen, so a word sounding the same is meant

parts.note: to block something is to stop it

explanation.surface: An alliance of nations bans a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of nations acting together politically, such as the old Soviet bloc.

clue.text: Comic writer making Port Said look ridiculous

indicators.note: the letters are made to look ridiculous by being jumbled up

parts.note: the city name is taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A satirist making fun of the Egyptian port city.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Said is a city at the northern end of the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parodist writes humorous imitations that mock the style of another work.

clue.text: Doctor chap is in surgery, finally working

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, reshaped into a new order

parts.note: these three words are taken letter for letter as fodder

parts.note: only the last letter of surgery is used

explanation.surface: A man is in the surgery at last, being seen to by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Surgery suggests a medical definition, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Physician is a formal word for a medical doctor.

clue.text: Certainly taken aback about most of calm positive image?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about, around, the shortened one
taken aback reads as being turned back, so the word runs in reverse

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: mild weather is calm

explanation.surface: Someone startled out of their calm into a more positive outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken aback means surprised in the surface, but here it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley is the cheerful smiling-face symbol, an image conveying a positive mood.

clue.text: Vegetable damage leading to argument

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a row is a noisy quarrel, rhyming with cow

explanation.surface: A spoiled crop in the garden sparks a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A marrow is a large green squash grown in British gardens, an overgrown courgette.

clue.text: Disrespectful comment concealed in Berlin's ultimatum

indicators.note: the letters are concealed inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Berlin's and the start of ultimatum

explanation.surface: A diplomatic slight tucked into a demand from the German government.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult is a rude remark meant to offend.

clue.text: Discussion group remains in disorder

indicators.note: the letters are left in disorder, scrambled into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word is taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A meeting stays chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small teaching class where students discuss a topic together.

clue.text: Rebuilt terminal is part of transport system

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt, put together in a fresh order

parts.note: the word is taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A refurbished station building forms part of the city network.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramline is a route or track along which trams run, part of urban transit.

clue.text: Notes openings for many University students in commerce

indicators.note: the openings are the first letters of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words is taken

explanation.surface: Lecture notes create opportunities for business students.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes looks like lecture notes, but it means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is made of notes played or sung in sequence.

clue.text: Millions reserve computer peripherals

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, reserve, as in an icy look

explanation.surface: Millions of devices kept back for computer users.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer mouse is a pointing device plugged into a machine; several are commonly called mice.

clue.text: Pessimist showing limits to civility, not entirely pleasant

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of civility are used

indicators.note: not entirely leaves the word short of its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.definitionFit: A cynic expects the worst of people and their motives, a gloomy outlook.

clue.text: Pretentious chap returned excellent type of tree

parts.note: a snob is someone pretentious about class or taste
A1 means first-rate; the digit 1 stands as the letter I

explanation.surface: A show-off came back with a superb specimen tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is a Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots; a tree grown this way is itself a bonsai.

clue.text: One paying to stay carrying article into part of camp

indicators.note: the article goes into the tent, inside it

parts.note: a tent is one of the shelters that make up a camp

explanation.surface: A paying guest at a campsite lugs an item into a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant pays rent to occupy a property owned by someone else.

clue.text: Leading trophy lifted

parts.note: pot is slang for a sporting trophy or cup

explanation.surface: The team in first place hoists the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Top as an adjective means foremost, in first position.

clue.text: Studies naval crime cabal?

definitions.note: a cabal is a secret group of plotters; the question mark flags that the answer is their plot

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
piracy is robbery at sea

explanation.surface: Is research into crime at sea a plotters' scheme?
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a group that plots in secret, and a conspiracy is both such a plot and the plotters.
